reasoning_traces.think:
Aleatoric forecasting involves predicting stochastic outcomes where correctness is undefined. Traditional reinforcement learning with realized outcomes introduces noise and overconfidence due to policy gradient corruption. The proposed solution uses a verifiable reward based on empirical win rates, which avoids noisy single outcomes and preserves reasoning chains. This reward, defined as $\mathcal{R}(p, \hat{p}(x)) = 1 - (p - \hat{p}(x))^2$, aligns forecasts with observed frequencies. Gradient masking ensures that reasoning remains intact during training, preventing overfitting to spurious correlations. The method achieves calibration comparable to betting markets without human supervision or fine-tuning, demonstrating a dual advantage: robustness to label noise and preservation of logical structure.
